title: Throughput-lane micropricing pilot with overflow insurance and grace-credit UX
creator: Sasha Mendes
description:
Objective: Validate a new packaging model that sells dedicated GPU capacity as discrete 'throughput lanes' with micropricing (per-lane/minute) and an optional overflow insurance product that covers spillover to preemptible or burst pools with guaranteed crediting on SLA degradation. This ticket scopes the pilot product spec, price buckets, contract clauses, console UX for grace credits, and the enterprise security questionnaire updates required for sale.

Hypothesis: Customers with spiky inference workload prefer predictable low-latency lanes billed at a linear MQ/minute rate and will pay a small premium (~8-12%) for an overflow insurance that provides cost-smoothing and automatic at-fault SLA credits when preemption causes throttling. Offering a 'grace-credit' UX reduces support tickets during high-variance weeks and increases conversion from trial to committed plans.

Scope:
- Define 3 throughput lane sizes (S/M/L) mapped to throughput units and token/sec targets.
- Design micropricing bands (per-lane per-minute rates), ramp discounts for 30/90/365 day commitments, and an optional overflow insurance add-on priced as % of committed spend.
- Contract language: SLA downgrade credit mechanics, preemption definitions, liability caps, data residency/KMS callouts for Private deployments.
- Console and billing UX: how grace credits surface in cost pages, real-time consumption meters, and opt-in workflow for insurance.
- Security & legal: update enterprise SQ template with questions about preemptible isolation, audit log retention for overflow events, and post-incident forensics SLAs.

Success metrics (pilot):
- 25% of targeted pilot accounts opt into overflow insurance within 60 days.
- <15% increase in Tier-1 support tickets per pilot account during high-variance weeks after grace-credit UX rollout.
- Clear unit economics: insurance attach rate yields at least +6% gross margin on dedicated bookings.

Acceptance criteria:
- Pricing matrix approved by Finance and Sales (sheet linked).
- Legal signs off on SLA credit mechanism and contract language variant.
- Console mockups implemented and validated with 3 pilot customers in UX sessions.
- Security questionnaire responses drafted for the new product flow and reviewed by Security (see attachments).

Planned rollout: 4-week internal pilot -> 8-week external pilot with 10 customers -> iterate and scope larger launch for dedicated-2026.04 release.

Notes on trade-offs:
- Selling per-minute lane granularity increases billing complexity; offset with a simplified per-day reconciliation job and an explicit minimum billing quantum for lane attachments.
- Overflow insurance reduces immediate revenue volatility but creates contingent credit exposure; modeled in finance workbook and constrained by liability caps in contracts.
